blocks.p: A note on this edition. This is Milton’s epic, line for line, in modern English. It keeps his form: unrhymed blank verse, ten syllables to the line, the same number of lines in every book as he wrote, so that any passage can be laid beside the original. The words and sentence order have been brought into the English of today, and the old pronouns are gone, while his images, his names, and his argument are kept whole; nothing has been added and nothing cut. Each book opens with Milton’s own prose summary, his “Argument,” in modern prose, and closes with brief notes on the classical, biblical, and geographical allusions a modern reader is least likely to know. The theology is Milton’s own and is rendered as he wrote it. Two passages Milton expanded for the 1674 edition (Book V, the angels’ feast; Book XI, the vision of disease and Adam’s reply) follow his expanded text, and one line dropped by the source transcription (Book XII, “By day a cloud, by night a pillar of fire”) has been restored.
